messages.author: 3ee48e66048494b3
messages.subject: Error when using slicing assignment to assign vector values to indexed matrix
parts:
Following Ben's solution at https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/kpkKWTvoEks I'm trying to assign a vector of parameters to an indexed subset of matrix entries. 

However I'm receiving a compilation error when I try to follow the method. This is replicable using a stripped down copy of Ben's code, attached along with R session info and full error message below. Any suggestions on the cause of the error message and/or workarounds greatly appreciated. Commenting out the line assigning Bvec to the matrix results in successful compilation.

R version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Ubuntu 16.04.2 LTS

other attached packages:
[1] rstan_2.14.1         StanHeaders_2.14.0-1 ggplot2_2.2.1

starting worker pid=29973 on localhost:11823 at 20:22:46.657
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

base type mismatch in assignment; variable name=B, type=matrix; right-hand side type=vector
Illegal statement beginning with non-void expression parsed as
  B[row_mark, col_mark]
Not a legal assignment, sampling, or function statement.  Note that
  * Assignment statements only allow variables (with optional indexes) on the left;
    if you see an outer function logical_lt (<) with negated (-) second argument,
    it indicates an assignment statement A <- B with illegal left

  * Sampling statements allow arbitrary value-denoting expressions on the left.
  * Functions used as statements must be declared to have void returns


ERROR at line 23

 21:      
 22:      matrix[3,3] B;
 23:      B[row_mark,col_mark] = Bvec;
          ^

  one node produced an error: failed to parse Stan model 'temp' due to the above error.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error when using slicing assignment to assign vector values to indexed matrix
parts:
int<lower=1,upper=3> row_mark[7];
int<lower=1,upper=3> col_mark[7];

vector[7] Bvec;

matrix[3,3] B;

B[row_mark,col_mark] = Bvec;


This won't work. B[row_mark, col_mark] is a matrix (not
a vector), with indexing defined by

B[row_mark, col_mark][i, j] = B[row_mark[i], col_mark[j]].

I'm not sure what you're trying to do with that fragment of code,
so I don't know what to recommend.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error when using slicing assignment to assign vector values to indexed matrix
parts:
Thanks. Would this method of assignment have worked in a previous version? The thread linked to in my original post and Ben's response seem to suggest so.

What I'm trying to achieve is a matrix with common priors on all entries, but with a a subset of entries fixed at pre-specified values. For example:

[X, 0, 0,
 X, 0, 0, 
 0, X, 0,
 0, X, 0,
 0, 0, X]

Where '0' entries are fixed at zero, and 'X' entries have prior N(0, 1). I suspect this could be achieved by simply specifying all matrix entries individually in the model, but was looking to see if there was a less verbose solution (in this case by using a vector of position indices).

a vector), with indexing defined by

I'm not sure what you're trying to do with that fragment of code,
so I don't know what to recommend.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error when using slicing assignment to assign vector values to indexed matrix
parts:
> On Feb 22, 2017, at 3:42 AM, Ewan Keith <ewan.k...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks. Would this method of assignment have worked in a previous version? The thread linked to in my original post and Ben's response seem to suggest so.

No. The Stan language has been fully backward compatible since
version 1.0 with a single exception---you can't access lp__ directly
any more.

The behavior with matrices is confusing for a lot of people, but
it's the same as the behavior in R.

> What I'm trying to achieve is a matrix with common priors on all entries, but with a a subset of entries fixed at pre-specified values. For example:
>
> [X, 0, 0,
> X, 0, 0,
> 0, X, 0,
> 0, X, 0,
> 0, 0, X]
>
> Where '0' entries are fixed at zero, and 'X' entries have prior N(0, 1). I suspect this could be achieved by simply specifying all matrix entries individually in the model, but was looking to see if there was a less verbose solution (in this case by using a vector of position indices).

Maybe you could do this in a less verbose way, but it wouldn't be
as clear. Given that it's not a submatrix, matrix slicing won't work.
You'd have to do something like this:

data {
int[5] is;

parameters {
vector[5] x_raw;

model {
vector[15] x_vec = rep_vector(0, 15);
matrix[5, 3] x;
x_vec[x_non_zero] = x_raw;
x = to_matrix(x_vec);

...

You could also define x as a transformed parameter, just make x_vec
a local variable inside { } because you don't want to save that.
And be careful of the order in to_matrix (I can't recall which order
we use).

- Bob
